title: Learned listening groups span country boundaries in a LastFM sample
summary: A fitted spectral-plus-k-means partition of 511 LastFM users identified groups spanning seven countries. Posthoc comparisons associated the learned groups with different listening breadth, activity and artist profiles. These are descriptive patterns in a selected historical sample, not universal listener types.
ai_technology: Sequential BiFLICKER spectral estimation; fitted k-means unsupervised clustering

evidence.tested: Seven learned groups from binary user–artist incidence; posthoc event-count summaries and leave-one-user-out intervals characterized the same sample.
evidence.unknown: Filtering removed low-degree users and very popular artists. Group number and genre interpretations are analysis-dependent. Breadth/artist profiles reuse clustering inputs; jackknife intervals and centralized agreement are not independent cohort validation. No causal country or preference claim.
evidence.ai_role: K-means fits latent assignments in a federated spectral embedding, enabling group-specific listening comparisons.

source_review.scope: Actual primary Methods3, LastFM Results6 and implementation/posthoc summariesS1; exact current v1 history.
